sections.heading: Types of insulin and storage
sections.paragraph:
"Doctor it's Ganesh's mother. I am calling from the medicine shop. You prescribed a yellow labelled insulin, but the shopkeeper is giving us a green labelled insulin and saying it is the same. What should I do?" Ganesh's mom asked in a confused voice.

Uneducated but smart mother of 4-year-old Ganesh takes care of her son's diabetes very efficiently. Often it is seen in the OPD that parents do not know which insulin they take and that the pharmacist is giving them the wrong insulin. All types of insulin lower blood sugar level but each insulin has a different way of working. Lack of awareness and using a different insulin can make the blood sugar level drop drastically or shoot up to avoid this situation and to have complete control over diabetes management you need to have basic information about all kinds of insulin available in the market.

Insulin Research&Formation: In January 1922, 14-year-old Lenard Thomson was given insulin first time and a new chapter began in the history of diabetes. The equation that Type 1 diabetes means death simply vanished. Since then in the last 100 years, a lot of changes happened in insulin production and in insulin delivery technique. Due to the developed biological system, pure insulin is available in large amount nowadays. With the changes in amino acid of insulin structure, designer insulins are developed. To inject insulin, disposable syringes, insulin pens, a less painful small needle (6mm/8mm) and insulin pumps are available nowadays. All these new treatment options are helping to make the life of children with T1D normal like other children.

Bolus and Basal insulin: in a healthy body after every meal, insulin is secreted through the pancreas, called bolus insulin. 3-4 hour after a meal slowly the release of insulin lowers down because blood sugar is also in control by then. Insulin reduces but does not end fully. In very less amount it always (24 hours) exists in blood, called basal insulin. (Due to this basal insulin, glucose level stay in the proper amount in fasting state too).

In keeping with this physiology, insulin is being produced in the laboratory with ongoing improvement with time. Insulin division is based on their onset and time of action. Short and rapid acting insulin is used as prandial/ meal (bolus] insulin. Intermediate and long-acting insulin is used as basal insulin. It is not necessary that in each child insulin action will be same. In fact, in the same child insulin action can vary at a different time and even on different days.

Different national and international medical companies manufacture insulin.

IDF has given colour code to all insulin for easy understanding among common people.

Types of insulin, colour codes and alternative insulin brands

1).Regular insulin (R) = On the bottle is a yellow label and this insulin looks clear like water. Many pharmaceutical companies manufacture this insulin with a different name. If you don't know all the names you can still identify this insulin by the yellow label. Insulin is measured in units. R insulin is available to us in 40 and 100 unit. It is difficult to understand the difference between both the vials without reading information printed on it. If you have 40-unit insulin, then youwill have to use red cap syringe and if you have 100-unit insulin then you will have to use orange cap syringe. This is an important thing to keep in mind.

Refill or cartridge in a pen is of 100 units. (If sometimes pen does not work then cartridge can be used with the 100-unit orange cap syringe) This insulin starts working after 30 to 45 minutes. So, if you want to match the blood sugar level and insulin you should take the insulin at least 30 minutes before your meal. Sometimes when post-meal sugar is high this gap itself can help you to control better. The effect of this insulin stays for 4-6 hours (Please note that in every child action curve of insulin may differ). Generally, every hour 15 to 20% insulin is consumed. For example, if you have injected 10 unit of R insulin then normally after 2-hours 40% insulin (4 unit) will be consumed, and 6 unit will be remaining. For this PP glucose test can be done after 3 hrs and not after 2 hours to know if more insulin is required or not. R insulin is affordable and available, but it should be taken a half-hour before the meal and its effect stays for a longer period, hence the need for newer insulins.

  1. Rapid-acting insulin is available in three forms Humalog, Novorapid and Apidra. All three insulins are 100-unit designer insulins available in pen and vials. This insulin starts working in 5-10 minutes. So, you can take this insulin before a meal, while eating and after finishing your meal. In young children, it is difficult to predict their food intake, and especially when they are sick, you can monitor their food intake and depending upon that you can fix insulin dose. The effect of this insulin lasts for 2-3 hours which reduces the chances of a late hypo. For best outcomes in PP blood sugar levels this insulin should be taken 15-20 minutes before a meal.

  2. Intermediate-acting insulin (NPH insulin) N insulin - This insulin's label is of green colour andlooks milky. Before taking this insulin gently roll the vial on your palm and make it homogeneous. If you shake the vial forcefully bubbles will come, and your dose of insulin can go wrong. This insulin starts working after 4-6 hours. Those children who cannot take insulin in school can take N insulin in the morning so that post-tiffin their sugar level does not increase. N insulin and R insulin can be given mixed together and is called split mix. With this method doses of both insulins can be altered as per requirement. For example, if there is a physical education class in school N insulin dose can be minimised. Effect of N insulin lasts for 12-13 hours. When N insulin is given as basal insulin at night then it is safe to have 1 or 2 biscuits before sleep. The peak of insulin reaches in 4-6 hours. So, it is necessary to check blood glucose around 2:00 to 3:00 AM because at that time chances of hypos are high.

In younger children, it is difficult to predict N insulin's action profile. Unexpected hypo can trouble any time making frequent glucose check the only safe option.

In combination with N insulin, rapid insulin and R insulin are available as premixed insulins in the market. (30/70 Mixtard, 25/75 Humalog mix, 30/70 Novolog mix)premixed insulin is normally not recommended for children as it takes away not only the flexibility of eating and playing but also shows great glycaemic variability. However, if needed, with proper guidance, this insulin can be used.

  1. Long-acting designer insulin is available in three forms Lantus, Levemir and Tresiba. The job of this insulin is to control fasting blood glucose level which means it works like basal insulin. It is important to have the correct dose of basal insulin. If your fasting blood glucose is in control and normal, then insulin dose throughout the day is correctly manageable. That is why we can call it our foundation insulin.

Lantus insulin is available as 100 unit in pen and while. You can fix the time of injection, but it is necessary to keep the same time every day. Lantus looks like water so you should not get confused with R insulin. Do keep this in mind. This injection can hurt sometimes because of its acidic nature. So, in young children injection should be given on backside on their seat so it should not pain as much. Lantus stays for 22-24 hour in blood. For most people one injection is sufficienthowever sometimes in young children, Lantus is divided into 2 doses.

Irrespective of Lantus injection time, to know the effect of Lantus, fasting blood glucose should be checked. In all recent studies, it has been seen that Lantus is safe in children.

Most of the time Levemir insulin is taken twice. In obese children with this insulin, weight can be better controlled. Tresiba is just launched and there are limited number of studies about the safety of this insulin in children. (Tresiba is 3 times costlier than Lantus.)

Most of the time one wonders which insulin is good for use and the answer is-One shoe does not fit all. The insulin which controls your diabetes is the best insulin for you. If you understand the working of insulin you can choose insulin as per your need. Your diabetes team will guide you regarding this.

Extra insulin can be stored in the fridge (not in freezer) till its expiry date.

Insulin which you are currently using can be kept outside at room temperature (area that does not heat up). In this insulin, comparatively no bubbles are formed, and it causes less pain. If the colour of insulin is changed or small particles or crust appears, then this insulin is damaged. The medical companies advise to change the insulin in use within a month. In young children and toddlers due to very small dose wastage of insulin may beseen. (One option to this situation is the availability of vial and pen with less ml of insulin.)

All insulin measurement is in the unit. If one unit of insulin lowers 50 mg blood sugar in your body, then every insulin's 1 unit will reduce the blood sugar by 50 mg. Only difference would be the time taken to do that. Rapid insulin will lower the blood glucose fast and long acting insulin wil lower the blood glucose slow. This knowledge will help you to adjust the dose of insulin and to have a better.

All insulin measurement is in the unit. If one unit of insulin lowers 50 mg blood sugar in your body, then every insulin's 1 unit will reduce the blood sugar by 50 mg. Only difference would be the time taken to do that. Rapid insulin will lower the blood glucose fast and long-acting insulin will lower the blood glucose slow. This knowledge will help you to adjust the dose of insulin and to have a better control of your diabetes!

sections.heading: Insulin injection technique
sections.paragraph:
"Doctor I don't know what has happened to Rohit's diabetes in last 3 months. His blood sugar is not controlled at all, sometimes very low and sometimes goes very high. Our family physician has suggested going for an insulin pump for better control. We thought of consulting you before taking the final decision. 10-year-old Rohit's father was in OPD after a year. Rohit's family was taking care of his diabetes very well. In fact, in the last 3 to 4 years he had no complications related to diabetes. For 10 years of age, in last one year, he had shown good growth as well. On studying his blood glucose record it was difficult to come to any conclusion.

In a diabetes clinic, it is important to check the insulin injection site while doing the physical examination of children. We found an abnormal mass of fat under the skin of Rohit's injection site on his thighs. Since the past few months, Rohit was taking his insulin shots by himself and this injection site did not hurt, so he did not bother to change the injection site. Repeated insulin injection in the same location or too much use of the same syringe can cause thickness in the skin and abnormal fat under the skin resulting in no sensation of injection and no pain. This is called Lipohypertrophy a commonly seen problem.

At this site injected insulin does not go into the blood properly. Sometimes it holds up at the same place causing an increase in blood glucose level and after some time the whole quantity of insulin goes into the blood at one go causing a sudden lowering of blood glucose. To prevent this kind of situation, change of insulin injection site and change of needle is important. By avoiding lipohypertrophy sites and injecting at other sites not only uncontrolled blood glucose can be controlled, but sometimes insulin requirement comes down as well. Lipohypertrophy can take 3 to 6 months to heal. The only solution is not to give the injection at that site. Due to analogue insulin and biological insulin, the injection site can show lipoatrophy. Comparatively very few incidences of this kind have been seen.

It is therefore important to have complete knowledge of insulin, insulin injecting technique, insulin storage technique and much more to be self-sufficient in diabetes management.

What is the right place to inject insulin?

Insulin is given under the skin in the fat [subcutaneous). By mistake, if insulin is given in skin it will hurt and can create a red swollen area. If by mistake it is given in veins, besides hurting it will lower the blood glucose extremely fast and can cause unexpected hypo. While giving insulin injection if blood comes or small bubbles go with insulin, it is not to be worried about.

acting (R) and intermediate acting (NPH) insulin can vary with their injection site depending on the site. Learn about and keep changing the injection site.

1. Buttocks- due to fat on the seat of children it is easy for their parents to inject there. The insulin given at this site goes slowly in blood. This site is best for long acting insulin (Lantus/ Basalog etc).

2. Abdomen-very delicately hold the fat on the abdomen and inject insulin. At this site, the insulin goes fast into the blood.

3. Upper arm -in young children try to avoid this site. And while injecting delicately hold the fat area, inject the needle in 45 degrees otherwise needle can go in the vein. At this site, the insulin goes in blood at a medium pace but faster than insulin injected on thighs.

4. Thighs-almost all children like to take insulin at this site.

During exercise, insulin gets observed in blood faster. So if you are going to play football, take insulin on arm and not on thighs. Similarly, if you are going to play tennis take insulin on thighs and not on arm. Another precaution is do not bathe with hot water or don't go into a hot water tub after taking insulin injection because hot water results in faster absorption of insulin in the blood which can cause hypoglycaemia.

sections.heading: Using a syringe, pen or pump
sections.paragraph:
Syringe 1 ml 40 IU (red cap, per 1-unit marking)

Syringe 1 ml 100 IU (orange cap, per 2-unit marking)

Insulin strength (40 unit/ml or 100 unit/ml) should match the same strength syringe.

If by chance you do not have 100-unit syringe and you are forced to take Lantus like insulin which is 100-unit insulin by 40-units syringe please note that you need to lower the Lantus dose by 2.5 times. For example, if your Lantus dose is 20 unit, witha 40 unit syringe your dose would be 20/2.5-8 unit. If you are not good in calculations, take a minimum dose of Lantus. It is important to avoid such mistakes for the sake of the safety of the child. Correct use of a syringe is always the best option.

With insulin pen, nowadays it is quite simple to inject insulin. An insulin pen is a blessing for children with fear of prick. All types of insulin are available in pen. Strength of insulin in pen is 3 ml and 100 unit/ml. Insulin injecting technique is the same as a syringe. You need to do priming of insulin pen before taking the injection and for priming, every time hold the pen upward, dial 2 unit and press the button. Only after this, dial your dose and inject yourself. Priming is important for 2 things, firstly to remove the air bubble in the needle so that the right dose of injection (insulin) is injected and secondly to ensure that insulin is coming out of the pen properly. Pens are available as 2 types- use and throw (Kwick pen-Lily/Flex pen-Nova/ Solo star-Sanofi) and reusable (Human, Novapen, Allstar). Almost all pens can give 1-70-unit insulin in one shot. Human LUXURA is available for injecting 0.5-unit insulin in young children. The needle of the pen comes in nano Page u mynt 71-6 milli roter) coin most of the children there is no need to hold the fat of skin and can be directly injected.

In some of the countries, I-Port or Insuflon is available for injecting insulin. This tiny cannula can be kept below the skin for 4 to 5 days and through that insulin can be injected.

Insulin pump is the most advanced option for insulin injection. There are a lot of positive changes happening in the insulin pump. In some of the developed countries on an experimental basis, the automatic pump has been given to children. These are called Bionic pancreas.

Diabetes team teaches you insulin injection technique and ensures that you have learned it. Some aspects need to be highlighted.

1. Every time ensure that you have taken correct insulin vial or pen. A common mistake found in OPD, instead of Lantus, R insulin has been injected in night.

2. NPH insulin to be shaken gently to make it homogenous and smooth.

3. If you are supposed to take NPH and R insulin together in the syringe, first take R insulin in the syringe then NPH insulin.

4. After injecting insulin hold for 10 seconds at least, then take out the needle from the skin. This ensures that insulin goes into the body fully. Sometimes the little amount of blood can come out but that is nothing to worry about.

5. While taking insulin from pen always do priming.

6. Keep changing insulin injection site appropriately and do not use the needle till it gets blunt.

You must be wondering that medical science is so advanced nowadays then why we do we not have oral insulin? Insulin is a protein and is inactivated by the digestive juices of the mouth and intestine. Few pharma companies are researching on oral insulin. Inhaled insulin as bolus insulin (Afrezza) may be available in the next few years. But to know the safety in Type 1 diabetes children it will take a lot of trials. You must have read about those researches in a magazine or social media but most of the time these are just trials. It is important to learn from your team about current diabetes management techniques very minutely. Being an expert in these techniques will benefit you lifelong.

sections.heading: Insulin regimen
sections.paragraph:
"Doctor there is protein in Shobha's urine, so we have come to you. Our village doctor told us that her diabetes is not controlled, and it can damage her kidney". Shobha's dad was anxious. Shobha was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at the age of 9. She is 17-year-old today. Her family always thought that 2 times pre-mix insulin injection is sufficient. Some days, due to complication and problems she used to get hospitalised, at that time doctors used to tell them about the increasing the number of insulin injection and frequent checking of blood glucose on glucometer but the family was against this. Actually, this unacceptance came from lack of awareness.

If blood glucose is not controlled well then after some years micro blood vessels fail and can cause deterioration of organs. When micro blood vessels of the kidney are affected then urine has small amount of protein (microscopic albuminuria). At this juncture, if blood glucose is controlled adequately and with the use of ACE inhibitor medicines then kidneys function can be restored. But if not controlled at the right time kidney may fail, resulting in high blood pressure. which may finally end up with dialysis or kidney transplantation. Diabetes team explained everything in detail to Shobha and her family. For better control of blood glucose basal and bolus insulin was started and every month she was called for a regular check-up in OPD.

When insulin was first discovered it was impure and doses and timing of insulin injection was decided by patients' symptoms. For example, frequent urination meant an insulin shot and in symptoms of hypo avoid insulin. Injection syringe and needle used to be quite big. After repetitive boiling, the needle used to get blunt which hurt the children and it was mental trauma for the family. But this was the only option to survive. Later new options became available in insulin, syringes, and needles to achieve minimal injection numbers.

Now once or twice in 24 hours insulin injections were being given but there was no clarity as to what is needed to control diabetes and have a normal life.

In 1993 DCCT (Diabetes Control and complications trial) published their research which dramatically changed type 1 diabetes management. Due to uncontrolled diabetes children had retinopathy which causes blindness, neuropathy, kidney failure and sometimes at a very young age heart attack or paralytic attack. After DCCT research those children who went through their guided diabetes management as given below had lesser complications.

1.3 to 4 times blood page check-Goat home by zlucometer.

2. Diet and exercise should be well planned.

3. Insulin injection need to be taken twice or more in a day. This was called multiple daily injections (MDI).

MDI regimen is just like insulin secreted in a healthy body. In this basal and bolus insulin concept was incorporated. Rapid-acting insulin for each meal as per need to be taken and one long-acting basal insulin without fail which will control fasting blood glucose. The insulin pump is also based on this theory. The only difference is that in this short or rapid-acting insulin injected digitally.

The benefits of MDI regimen are undisputed but practically in some children trial and error needs to be done to fix the insulin regimen (number of insulin injection per day). Family support is the centre point of diabetes treatment. If 3 to 4 times insulin injection is not acceptable to the family then mutually insulin regimen needs to be finalised. In this kind of situation, a group discussion can be helpful. These children need to be handled sensitively. Any kind of insulin regimen used should be based on the concept of basal and bolus insulin.

Basal insulin: Healthy pancreas secrets insulin 24 hours that is called basal insulin. Body cells require this basal insulin to convert glucose secreted from the liver into energy. If by any reason basal insulin is not secreted blood sugar will shoot up suddenly. Then the job of basal insulin is to control fasting blood glucose (in between meals and in sleep) and when you are not doing any exercise. Hence it is important to have the correct dose of basal insulin to control your diabetes. Basal insulin requirement varies from person to person. You will have to fix your basal dose by frequent checking of blood glucose on the glucometer.

Some observations have been made after examining children in different age groups.

1. Basal insulin is required mostly in the night especially after 3:00 AM till 10:00 AM It is called dawn phenomena. At this time counter-regulatory hormones which work against insulin are secreted. If your sleeping time blood sugar is normal but, in the morning, fasting blood glucose is high, ir baral inculin doce if in afternoon basal insulin requirement is less, then maybe in the daytime your physical activity is helping you to increase the action of insulin.

2. Young people need (till 21 yr.) more basal insulin due to sex hormones. Young children below 10 years need more basal insulin in the evening which is called as dusk phenomena. After 60 years, the dose of basal insulin lowers down drastically.

You can use NPH insulin (Insulatard) as basal insulin, its effect stays for 12 to 14 hours. In blood this insulin's level is not constant. After 4 to 6 hour it increases causing chances of hypo. After taking bedtime N insulin it is particularly important to check blood sugar level after 4 to 6 hours. In young children, severe hypo can happen. New designer basal insulin (Lantus, detemir and Tresiba) stays at a constant level in blood so chances of a hypo are very less.

Bolus insulin: The other partner in insulin regimen is bolus insulin which needs to be taken as per meal. There are a lot of things to be considered while fixing the dose of bolus insulin. First check your blood glucose level before a meal then calculate carbohydrates in your meal and depending upon these 2 things consult your dietician to fix your bolus insulin dose. Dr Davidson has given a formula in 1980 to know either 1-unit insulin lowers how much blood glucose or 1-unit insulin lowers how many carbs.

Insulin: carb ratio = 500/required insulin in 24 hrs (If your total requirement of basal and bolus insulin is 25 unit then by this formula 500/25 20. This means for 20-gram carb in your food 1-unit insulin is required.)

Insulin sensitivity factor (correction ratio) =1500 for short-acting insulin and 1800 for rapid-acting insulin/insulin required in 24 hours (if your total insulin requirement is 25 basal plus bolus then the calculation should be 1500/25=60. that means to reduce 60-milligram glucose, 1-unit insulin is required.)

The most important thing is not that these formulas are absolutely correct, but this may be used as stepping stones. You can start with this formula or calculation and for each Page 4 t/s 10 carton Quot For food items with on labels you can take help of nutritionist to calculate insulin: carbs.

The most important thing is not that these formulas are absolutely correct, but this may be used as stepping stones. You can start with this formula or calculation and for each person, this calculation will differ. For food items with nutrition labels, you can take help of nutritionist to calculate insulin: carb ratio. Keeping a food diary and the blood sugar levels after different meals, you can learn to bolus accurately.

Giving your child the pleasure of different food without compromising in diabetes control is essential part of management.

sections.heading: How many injections a day, and working out the dose
sections.paragraph:
1. Twice or thrice in a day this insulin regimen was popular between 1980 to 1990. In this R insulin (Actrapid or Insugen R yellow labelled) and insulin NPH (Insulatard/Insugen N green label) were mixed and given. Later, pre-mix insulin was available in different strength (Mixtard Brown label 30/70&50/50). This premixed insulin is quite easy to use and affordable so use of these increased. These insulins are still in use for type 1 children. The only problem with premix insulin is children have a variable daily routine. Children's game, food keeps changing so the insulin in which changes as per need is not possibly makes good control of diabetes difficult. Blood sugar can go up and down very erratically. In developed countries in order to give children optimum development, this insulin is almost obsolete.

R and N insulin mixed in syringe are called a split mix pattern. There is some flexibility in this regimen, so to some extent controlling diabetes is possible. However, with twice day split mix insulin, trying to control diabetes without hypoglycaemia becomes stressful for parents. Also, one cannot vary the diet too much leading to frustration.

N insulin taken before dinner reaches its peak in blood in 4 hours which can cause hypo or N insulin levels are very less in blood by morning so fasting blood glucose before breakfast may be on the higher side. In this situation, if you take insulin before sleep rather before dinner it may give a little better result. In fact, this insulin regimen is also not a complete solution. Many times, when children do not accept their diabetes in beginning because of this trial and error, the diabetes team should accept their insulin regimen and guide the family.

  1. MDI (multiple day injections): In this regimen before every main meal bolus insulin is to be injected. To fix the bolus insulin -

A. Pre-meal blood glucose level

B. Carb count in meal

C. Play and exercise

Your day to day life will be easier if you fix the insulin dose keeping in mind all these variables.

1. Your pre-meal blood glucose is 250. You require 1-unit insulin to reduce 50-milligram glucose (sensitivity ratio) and your pre-meal blood glucose target is 120 to 150.

250-150-100 milligram. More than 100-milligram glucose-lowering

100/50-2 Unit insulin will bring your pre-meal to normal.

2. There are 60-gram carbohydrates in the meal.

You require 1-unit insulin to cover 15-gram carb (I:C ratio)

60/15-4-unit insulin will bring your post-meal glucose to normal.

If the child is fond of playing you need to lower down the insulin dose on trial and error method. In beginning all these things may seem tough but as time goes you become habitual to it and it becomes really easy. Diabetes team plays a very important role to make them understand all these aspects to make life normal for the child.

N insulin or Lantus/Tresiba/detemir can be given as basal insulin before sleep. Most of the children need detemir twice a day. Pharma companies suggest not mixing Lantus and bolus insulin. (Unofficially these were mixed but it did not make much difference in insulin dose). To fix basal insulin dose, keep a record of before sleep and fasting blood glucose for a few days. If the insulin dose is correct, then 30-50 milligram blood glucose changes can be seen.

If morning blood glucose is normal, then it is easy to control the whole day's blood glucose. Which means your basal insulin dose needs to be perfect. If in the night 8 to 12 hours child's blood glucose is in control that means a child can stay in a normal glucose level for 40 to 50% time. This all leads to normal growth. for them. Sometimes PP glucose is normal in glucose record, but Pre-meal blood glucose level is high. In this condition, basal insulin dose can be divided into 2 parts and be given twice daily. This will usually solve the problem

Insulin pump

In this bolus insulin is taken with due calculation as in MDI regime. By pressing a small button, bolus insulin can be injected as per need. Blood glucose level can be kept normal by giving bolus insulin more than 4 times. In MDI regimen once released basal insulin can't be revert but in insulin pump we can change in basal insulin dose as well as if need be basal insulin can be stopped for some time too. Using an insulin pump without having complete knowledge can be stressful and give you an adverse reaction and sometimes you may face a serious problem. Discuss all the insulin regimen with your diabetes team, depending upon that you can decide and in fact can change your decision anytime. Choose the insulin regimen which suits best to your lifestyle and control your diabetes carefully.

Source: Dr. Kalpana Jog (MD-Pediatrics), T1D Consultant, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. Originally published in ‘Madhumitra’, a magazine of the Diabetic Association of India.

sections.heading: Advantages of an insulin pump
sections.paragraph:
There is research going on in the world-renowned Joslin Diabetes Centre in Boston on Gold Medalist persons with Type 1 diabetes (people who have had type 1 diabetes at least 50 years). Not many complications are seen in these Type 1 gold medalists who are now more than 70 years old. They are around 1000 in number. Dr George King and his colleagues are researching how these Type 1 patients managed their diabetes and have not shown any diabetes complications like other patients.

According to George King, a significant point noted in the research was “These Type 1 people definitely have a different vision. They are focused on regular exercise; conscious diet and these self-motivated persons know that their diabetes is their responsibility. They are aware of new research in the diabetes field. The primary focus in their early days of their available diabetes management was to keep them alive. As new research came up and new technology developed in the diabetes field, this group of Type 1 patients also updated themselves by having complete information about it. Some of them take insulin injection 3 or more time, some of them check blood glucose at a regular interval, some of them are on the insulin pump and some of them use CGMS. A single factor that stands out is that they all know that “diabetes is their own responsibility" and having accepted the treatment modality, they do not find age a barrier in updating themselves to new technology.

There is not a single technique in diabetes management which is impeccable or complete till date. Insulin pump too has its own benefit and disadvantages.

Actually, the pump’s benefits also depend upon the user’s mindset. Those children who prick themselves 6-7 time in a day, they feel good with the insulin pump, as pricking is minimized. Whereas the parents feel good about relaxation in the child’s food restrictions.

Benefits of insulin pump that were seen in research:

Improvement in blood glucose control

Those children and families who started using an insulin pump with adequate understanding, 0.5-1% improvement in HbA1c has been see more than that the glucose variability was minimized. So, long term complication of diabetes may be prevented.

Incidences of hypos was less

The important benefit of Insulin pump is the great lowering of hypo incidences. For this, some management is needed (think ahead), regular blood glucose test and depending upon that adjusting insulin dose and taking proper diet. In modified pump blood glucose sensor is connected to the pump, so as soon as low sugar happens pump stops releasing insulin and gives a signal to the child. The moment blood glucose level increases pump starts again. It is necessary to fix the blood glucose sensor with a pump, but it’s quite a costly affair.

3.Easy availability of insulin

The most important benefit of the insulin pump is having insulin with you 24 hrs, and in any situation, it can be given to you without any obstacle. By only pressing button insulin can be taken so especially young children enjoy this benefit the most. Ups & downs of blood glucose level during exercise or playing can be stabilized by the option of stopping or adjusting insulin dose in the pump. This is a great benefit. Liberty of sleeping till late in the morning without an increase in blood glucose is possible with the insulin pump.

4.Post meal blood glucose control is easy

There is uncertainty in young children’s food habit. In that situation, it is difficult for the child’s mother to fix the insulin dose. But with the pump’s bolus feature, it is easily possible. As per the Insulin pump’s wizard, it is easy to fix the insulin dose for different food items.

sections.heading: Disadvantages of an insulin pump
sections.paragraph:
In Insulin pump basal insulin-releasing technique is automatic but for bolus insulin, it has to be fixed carefully. Basal insulin controls blood glucose secreted in body but if you forget to take insulin for the meal then HbA1c may increase. These are a few reasons for the failure of the insulin pump. For this there is an alarm system in the pump, if you miss your insulin at the specific time of the meal, it will alert you.
If by any reason insulin is not delivered through the pump, then insulin in the body finishes in 2 hours and ketone body formation starts in Type 1 child’s body. If not controlled in time a serious situation like DKA can happen. There are many reasons for non-delivery of insulin through the pump. Sometimes there is a blockage in the pipe through which insulin delivered. Sometime cannula comes out of body or there is a small obstacle in cannula resulting in insulin falling outside. Due to preservative (phenols) in pump insulin gets a peculiar smell. You need to recognize this smell so that you can identify insulin leak out of the body. You are using insulin pump but if your blood glucose is unexpectedly high (>300), frequency of urine is more; thirstiness has also increased then immediately check your urine ketones. Depending upon that adjust your insulin dose and take it by syringe or pen. And change the whole cannula set. Child and parent should know about this otherwise the child or parent will press button of pump for delivery of insulin, which may not happen, and the child can get into a serious problem.
Due to use of pump good control of blood glucose is achieved and which help in increase in weight of the child. Just by pressing a button insulin gets delivered in the body so some children start eating unnecessarily too which may result in unexpected weight gain and may cause some other problems. So before using Insulin pump, talk to your dietician to have a check on your body weight.
Possibility of infection at the site of pump’s cannula quick set and sometime this infection may lead to abscess formation which may take time to heal. You can minimize this condition by keeping the injection site clean and changing cannula in 3-4 days. But sometimes you may need to use a different type of cannula (Sure-T/Silhouette)
In some of the sports or while swimming you need to keep your pump outside. Take care of the pump’s temperature in that condition. Insulin should not get hot or too cold, otherwise, insulin working will be affected.
It is said that using an insulin pump means learning new diabetes management. Training for the insulin pump is not easily available everywhere. In fact, sometimes without proper training pump may give you adverse results.
Insulin pump is the latest technology in insulin injections. But it is costlier than pen/syringe. Every 3-4 days cannula needs to be changed, which is also costly. Consider these factors and then only decide about Insulin pump.

In short, there are benefits and some challenges with the insulin pump. Family’s diabetes management will be a happy one if they consider and plan before using the insulin pump.

sections.heading: Insulin pump – basics of basal insulin
sections.paragraph:
“Doctor, my HbA1c was constantly high, it caused a skin infection. I underwent an operation. Blood glucose control should be good for the wound to heal, so our doctor told me to use an insulin pump. But now after 3 months HbA1c is back to 12… I do not understand what is wrong…” said Amol, showing the report. I am taking insulin as much you suggested, I did not change any of my programs, but how did such a report come?”

The answer to why Amol's report is like that was in his question itself. After installing the insulin pump in addition to insulin doses, the program also needs to be frequently changed depending upon frequent blood sugar tests. Often this information is not well understood or there is no self-confidence to do the changes.

Installing an insulin pump is like learning diabetes treatment new. The logbook brought by Amol was filled with fasting hypos and his reaction to that was to turn off the pump immediately or eating sugar. “When do you start the pump again?” answer was “when I remember to or when glucose is too high!” The basal insulin dose needed to be changed as per Amol’s blood glucose chart. The insulin pump is a state-of-the-art insulin delivery system, but the rules are the same as basal-bolus insulin.

sections.heading: Difference between injection and pump basal insulin
sections.paragraph:
Every minute, a small amount of insulin is supplied to the body from the pump (units of insulin per hour) is called the basal rate. Even in a healthy body, insulin is secreted from the pancreas in this manner. The purpose of this basal insulin is to control the glucose produced from the liver. And to keep the glucose stable during the fasting period or between two meals. Basal insulin causes the cells in the body to use the glucose from the liver for energy, therefore the production of energy from fats remains in control.

Many people are on multiple daily injections (MDI) of insulin before using pump and bolus & basal insulin are different. (Basal insulin: LANTUS / BASALOG /LEVEMIR/TRESIBA). In the pump, however, basal and bolus insulin is the same. Short-acting or Rapid-acting insulin acts as both - the basal and bolus. The biggest advantage of basal insulin in the pump is that you can keep different basal rates at different times. On injections, the dose of basal insulin cannot be changed once taken. Due to the temporary basal rate feature of the pump, temporarily basal insulin can be taken less/more and can be stopped as well.

sections.heading: How is the dose of basal insulin determined?
sections.paragraph:
The dose of basal insulin should be decided in consultation with your doctor. Initially, when the pump trial is run with saline instead of insulin, this dose is determined. In general, 80% of the child's total daily insulin dose (bolus + basal) is the insulin dose for the pump. Sometimes the same dose or 75% of basal injection (LANTUS etc.) dose can be taken as basal in the pump.

The hourly rate Is calculated by dividing the dose over 24 hours. In a healthy body, basal insulin levels are not constant. Day and night, morning and evening basal insulin changes according to the circadian rhythm. Studying this and setting some basic rules in initial days helps set basal insulin in the pump. Your Diabetes team is aware of your glucose control so, changes can be made as needed using following rules.

Rule 1: Blood glucose levels are low after midnight until 4 a.m. Therefore, the basal rate in the pump is kept low/half (e.g. if the hourly rate is 1-unit/hr then 12-4 am should be 0.5/hr)

Rule 2: Blood glucose level is elevated from 4-8 am this is called Dawn phenomena. Meanwhile, due to counter-regulatory hormones secretions in the body, glucose is produced in large amount from the liver. To control blood glucose level, basal insulation levels are to be increased. Accordingly, the basal rate in the pump is kept above the hourly rate or one and half time more. Often the result of these hormones can stay after breakfast also so you can keep this rate up to 10 o’clock. Dawn Phenomena, apparently occurs in adolescents and young adults (if the hourly rate is 1-unit/hr then till 4-10 am 1.5 units/hr)

Rule 3: Can keep the basal rate as the hourly rate from 10 am – 12 midnight. (If the hourly rate is 1-unit/hr, use the same in pump). Increased glucose levels are observed in young children or school-going children in the evening, i.e. before dinner is called Dusk phenomena. The exact reason is not known but may becounter-regulatory hormones secreted at this age. In such a case, the basal insulin rate in the pump needs to be increased after 6 pm onwards.

Rule 4: Everyone’s basal insulin need is different so, check the blood glucose regularly. If possible use CGMS to keep adjusting basal insulin dose.

As mentioned earlier, this is just the beginning, more changes are expected with time, but children and parents need to be involved when this basal rate is being set up. Diabetes can be controlled only if basal insulin is appropriate. At the beginning of the pump trial, if you understand the technique from the company’s representative well enough and if you try this yourself, then parents or children will not get fumbled by the pump.

Always keep in mind; you are primarily responsible for managing your diabetes!

sections.heading: Why checking blood sugar matters
sections.paragraph:
"Doctor, Aniket's report" Aniket's mom handed over all the medical reports to the doctor. "First, see my annual school report!" Aniket, with a great sense of pride, handed over his school report to the doctor. Aniket was 14-year-old, in 8th standard and had passed in all his papers. His medical reports were also good with HbA1c of 8.5%. He was diagnosed at the age of 12, but due to his poor financial condition and being from a remote village in Konkan, he was not able to get right medical supervision from any doctor. One year ago, when he had come in theOPD, he did not know anything about diabetes except taking insulin twice a day. Repeatedly, he used to get admitted ingovernment hospital in critical condition. His growth had also stalled. Although he wanted to study but due to frequent hospitalisation and lack of attendance in school, he could not pursue his studies.

These kinds of situations are common for children with T1D. To change this situation self-competency is a must in diabetes management. And in the process of being self-competent, "Glucometer" is your best friend.

Until a few years back, blood sugar was examined through urine samples. But there were so many complications in doing that and the results were not perfect as well. In the last 30 to 40 years advanced technologies have changed the face of diabetes management. "Gluometer" is a gift by which you can check your sugar level anytime anywhere very easily.

During 1983-1993, the Diabetes Control and Complication Trial (DCCT) was conducted on people with T1D in America and Canada. The outcome of that trial shows that better diabetes control is possible in T1D if these 3 things followed.

Frequent blood sugar testing on glucometer
Insulin injection to be taken2-4-times
Following a proper diet

If diabetes is controlled, growth of a child with T1D is normal like other children.

Trial outcome also shows that if in initial years of T1D Diabetes Management is proper then a child can live a long healthy life with less complications of Diabetes. For that Glucometer is going to be your best friend.

sections.heading: How to choose a glucometer
sections.paragraph:
Strips should be affordable and easily available in the market. Most of the time it is seen that glucometer is being given free but matching strips are very costly.
Required blood drop on the strip for sugar check should be very tiny and it should be taken up through capillary action as it’s really difficult for younger children to place their blood drop on the strip.
Glucometer should have a memory (at least 100 records).
Data from glucometer should be easily downloadable on the computer.
Glucometer should be simple to use. Date/Day/Time/Year should be simple to set in glucometer.

Lancet comes with a glucometer, which can be used to prick the finger lightly to get a blood drop. To adjust the length of the pricking needle, there is a dial in the lancet. When used with younger children, the dial should be at 1 or 2. If the needle is longer than it can hurt children. Before using lancet wash your hands properly (if possible, with lukewarm water) and dry them. If by any chance there is a food particle on finger, blood sugar can be on the higher side. Do not wipe your fingers with spirit. Even if a very small amount of spirit stays on your finger, the result on the meter may be incorrect. Too much use of spirit on your finger can damage the softness of your finger and it can become rough and hard enough to hurt you. When you are out of home keep spirit free wipes with you. To get a blood drop from your finger it should be pricked on the side of a finger, neither in the middle and nor on top (Figure -1).

When blood from a finger is taken by squeezing the finger, fluid from the tissue can mix with blood but it causes incorrect blood sugar reading on the glucometer. Children like to use the same finger for the prick, but it causes

Damage to the tissue of that finger and it starts hurting. So, use a different finger daily for blood sugar checking. You can use the fingers of your feet as well and the mid lower portion of your thumb too.

In some glucometers there is facility of alternate site testing. That means you can take blood from different part of body, normally the pain is bare minimum.

Keep two things in mind while taking blood from these sites. Firstly, keep the dial of lancet on 4 to 5, secondly, when you are in doubt of hypoglycaemia do not take blood from these sites as correct reading is hard to achieve.

Glucometer and strips should not be kept at too cold or too hot places. Keep them at room temperature. While in travel keep in mind that glucometer and strips should not get heated up. Do not keep them in the fridge.

The glucometers which required coding, match the code with the code on the bottle of strips. Sometimes it happens that you have a glucometer, but you are not aware of how to use the glucometer and what to do with the information from it.

sections.heading: Why children with T1D need frequent checks
sections.paragraph:
The first question is – Why do children with Type 1 Diabetes need frequent blood sugar checking?

The most important thing is “your safety”. It is impossible to know blood sugar levels from outside. It is not necessary that every time symptoms would be seen of low or high sugar. Especially in younger children it is very uncertain. Parent must check blood sugar of their child before sleep at night (bedtime). If sugar level is 130-150 mg/dL (in younger children 180 mg/dL) then late night chance of hypo is less. If correct insulin dose has been taken, then in night (empty stomach) normally 30-50 mg fluctuation is seen. (if while sleeping blood sugar is 160 mg/dL then in morning fasting blood sugar can range 130-180 mg/dL). Possibility of late-night hypo is high in younger children. Many times, we come to know about this only when child goes into convulsions. Such a situation can be avoided if you take good care of the child from the beginning itself.
After lot of studies, it is found that at least 4 times sugar check in a day can minimise the complications of Diabetes in children. Blood sugar check, before & after meal can tell you a lot of things. It is easy to titrate the dose of insulin if you come to know about impact of your food on your blood sugar. If you can control your diabetes, your motivation level also increases.
Biggest benefit of diabetes management is that you start living a normal life. You slowly come to know that there are lot of daily routine activities which can impact your blood sugar. For example, sports, exercise, exam, travel, few medicine, menstrual cycle of girls, weather change etc. With the help of a glucometer, you come to know the correct sugar level and you can prepare yourself (Think Ahead Strategy).
When there was no glucometer, children used to get hospitalized with every episode of hypo or hyperglycaemia. There was no way to find out what is happening inside body. But with glucometer now you can plan everything. So many times, you see the symptoms of hypoglycaemia but when you check your blood sugar level, it does not show low blood sugar. This is because if blood sugar level comes down extremely fast (300-200-100), you feel like it is a hypo. Hence with the help of glucometer you can take right decision. Blood sugar & ketones can increase when you are sick. In this kind of situation, you can avoid serious complications by checking your blood sugar frequently.

Self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG) has a very important place in your diabetes management. Due to SMBG, a child can pursue a better career in future. Nowadays, there are new machines (CGMS) which can check your blood sugar every 5 minutes.

In your day to day diabetes management at least 4 times blood sugar check is a must. Before each meal like before breakfast, before lunch, before dinner and particularly important is before sleep at night. All these sugar checks can help you to decide the correct dose of Insulin. In the last few years irrational restrictions in meals have been removed from children’s daily routine and a normal meal like other children has been added. It is called Dose Adjusted For Normal Eating (DAFNE).

There is a lot of variety in Indian food which causes changes in blood sugar. So, to know which food product is responsible for how much change in blood sugar post meal (after2-3 hr) sugar check is necessary to know the correct dose of insulin. Play, exercise can also cause blood sugar changes, so in school while in PT class, before game start, during game and post-game blood sugar check can improve diabetes management. It has an impact on performance of child.

sections.heading: Keeping blood sugar records
sections.paragraph:
Keeping all the blood sugar records is necessary because these records can

Guide for better judgement. (Chart 1)

If there is no one educated in house, then it is difficult to interpret the blood sugar readings on glucometer. In this situation if there are 2 digits (50) on meter it is understood that blood sugar is low. And if if there are 3 digits then seeing the first digit insulin dose is being corrected. If there is ‘HI’ on meter that means >600 and if there is ‘LO’ that mean <40 or data is not recordable. Many times, lack of knowledge can lead to misunderstanding. If family is unable to understand data on meter, Diabetes team needs to work like a teacher. In diabetes treatment lot of things need to be taken care of. Keeping blood sugar level in control is a fine balance, specially avoiding hypoglycemia.

American Diabetes Association had made different guidelines depending upon age which were changed in 2015.

sections.heading: Blood sugar target range and HbA1c
sections.paragraph:
(American Diabetes Association, 2015)

Diabetes Team should interact with Type 1 Diabetes child and her family to set the target range of blood sugar. Normally in SMBG record 65%-time blood sugar stays in range. Even after much effort 10-12% time hypoglycaemia and 25%-time hyperglycaemia can occur.

In these situations, none of the family members should give a negative comment, rather they should support the child. Frequent blood sugar checking gives crucial information and commenting in negative way on those data can lead to psychological rejection a feeling that glucometer is not her friend. It is not necessary that blood sugar will always be normal in spite of all the proper steps taken.

Please keep this serenity prayer with you from Diabetes team.

God grant me the serenity

To accept the things I cannot change;

Courage to change the things I can;

And wisdom to know the difference!

Source: Dr. Kalpana Jog (MD-Pediatrics), T1D Consultant; Diabetes Unit Team, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. Originally published in ‘Madhumitra’, a magazine of the Diabetic Association of India.

sections.heading: What is hypoglycaemia?
sections.paragraph:
"Doctor today I brought Mahesh to your children OPD"- Mahesh's mother said with hesitation. Mahesh is 25-year-old, he was detected with diabetes when he was 10 years old. The entire family took care of him very patiently and carefully. For the last 5-6 years, he was visiting the adult OPD. "His sugar is not at all in control, all the time it is high. He does not adjust his insulin dose, his HbA1c is more than 13%. Mahesh, you only talk to the doctor. I am going out." Saying this Mahesh's mother went out.

Mahesh took his own time to speak "Doctor I work in a company at a very reputed and responsible post. After joining my job, I had 2-3 severe episodes of hypo without any known cause. My colleagues who work under me hospitalized me. Now I am bored with these repetitive hypos and hospitalization. So now I do not bother about controlling my diabetes. With high sugar, there will be a problem in the future, but a hypo is the "Now" situation". With these hypos my present, my career will be finished. I am losing control over myself; it is very scary doctor. I hate it." Mahesh was irritated.

What Mahesh was doing was unacceptable, but we must understand that controlling Type 1 diabetes is tough. A little awareness can avoid any serious condition. The diabetes team had a session with Mahesh and tried to probe deeper into his daily routine to understand the challenges he might be facing. Mahesh identified problem areas like his new gym, food in the office, not disclosing to people that he is a Type 1 diabetic. He realised that he needed to make some lifestyle changes.

There are 2 major problems in diabetes management. First, severe diabetic ketoacidosis due to less or insufficient insulin and second, severe hypoglycaemia due to more than required insulin intake.

Doctor Elliott Joslin (1869-1962) called as the father of modern diabetes treatment passed a legislation- "Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis kills the patient and recurrent hypoglycaemia ruins the patient. So the patient who knows the most lives longest and patient education is not one of the treatments, but it is the treatment."

In Type 1 diabetes there is no alternative to insulin, and we cannot deny the fact that insulin causes hypo. If you learn how to minimize hypo or how to prevent severe hypo you can have a long and happy life as per Dr Joslin.

It is difficult to explain exactly at what level of glucose in the blood, symptoms of hypo appear. Most of the times if glucose is above 50-60 you do not see any symptoms but we can tell that you do have hypos. Let us understand that if your glucometer shows your reading less than 100 and your symptoms are gone after taking glucose or carbs then for sure you had a hypo.

A simple explanation of hypo is the amount of blood glucose used by the body is not fulfilled by the liver or your food intake. So, what is the reason behind this imbalance?

sections.heading: Causes of hypoglycaemia
sections.paragraph:
1. Higher insulin dose resulting in stoppage of glucose secretion from the liver and more use of blood glucose by muscle and fat.

  2. No food or less food intake.

  3. Exercise without prior planning or long hours of play especially in young children.

In a healthy body, there are two hormones that maintain blood glucose level between 70-140. In one group there is only insulin which lowers the sugar and does not allow blood glucose to cross its limit. In another group there are 4 hormones known as "counter-regulatory hormones" which increase the do not allow blood glucose to go too low.

When blood glucose drops to 70 then glucagon and adrenalin enter in blood.

(Adrenalin-You must have heard this name about brave players.) Release of these hormones help the glucose to enter the blood stream and the body gets notified with some symptoms. Added to this, sometimes growth hormones and cortisol are also released which cause glucose secretion from the stored fat in the liver and this process is called gluconeogenesis. Effect of these hormones stays for a long period of time.

All these hormones cumulatively work to keep blood glucose in the normal range. Another important point is that when glucose level goes down, insulin secretion almost stops. But opposite to this in diabetes, when your blood glucose goes down (we learned a simple explanation). Glucagon is not released immediately. In fact in all Type 1 children deficiency of Glucagon is seen. So, the responsibility of increasing glucose level in the blood goes to adrenalin. If you are having recurrent hypos, adrenalin quantity also lowers down with time. So when needed in an emergency, adrenalin fails to respond in time. When blood glucose level goes to 40-50mg/dl, adrenalin is released and emergency symptoms are missed.

Insulin levels in blood totally depend upon the time and dose of insulin you have taken so even if you are in a hypo, insulin is still active in the body. Conscious blood glucose testing or immediate action after any symptoms can only prevent severe hypo incidences.

sections.heading: Symptoms of hypoglycaemia
sections.paragraph:
When blood glucose level goes <70 following symptoms are seen:

  1. Feeling hungry

  2. Shivering

  3. Heart palpitation

  4. Sweating

  5. Tingling

sensation in the body.

Adults can and handle this situation without any help but the problem arises with young children or toddlers. The symptoms may not always be noticed by their caregiver. Hypoglycaemia is identified usually during the OPD visits. At their age, their behavioural change can be the only symptom. Toddlers may get cranky and end up crying unusually and then their symptoms are only recognized by their mothers. With proper guidance and understanding these young children can learn to recognize the symptoms of hypoglycaemia. Timely action can prevent severe hypo. 15-20-gram sugar can bring the blood glucose levels to normal within 15-20 minutes.

When blood glucose level goes <50, then only mental unresponsiveness is seen.

1. Young children feel confused; they do not understand what is going in their class. 2. Decision-making capacity is hampered 3. Sleepiness 4.

Fatigue/tiredness

In all these situations children may need help. Sometimes children cannot eat food given to them, so it is important to make sure that they eat. This is called moderate hypoglycaemia. At least 2 times 15-20 gram sugar is needed to bring down the blood glucose level to normal in 15-20 minutes but to be completely stable it takes little more time.

By any reason, if glucose level goes down further then it is called severe hypoglycaemia and it may result in complete loss of brain control. Symptoms are -1. Children become violent suddenly 2. Stammer 3. Confused and uncontrolled 4. Unconscious

In all these situations children need urgent help for sure. If help comes from a person with a medical background, then the situation can be controlled timely. Immediate treatment in this kind of situation is intravenous glucose injection or Glucagon injection. Once glucose level gets normal it can again go down, so it is important to keep a watch. It can take 24 hours or more to be physically or mentally normal. In some children, hemiparesis can happen. There is no need for any kind of test as complete improvement is possible within a few hours only. Hypos while sleeping is a nightmare for children and their parents.

Hypoglycaemia can be easily prevented by daily glucose monitoring. The dawn phenomenon which occurs between 2:00-3:00 am often leads to moderate to severe hypoglycaemia if the bed-time sugars are not managed well.

Symptoms like hunger, sweatiness, headache or toddler wake up crying are not always visible, and a hypo may occur without any visible symptoms. Night-time hypos are commonly seen in children. Children who play a lot experience night-time hypos most of the time which is unexpected for them. While playing muscle needs glucose which is fulfilled by the liver (adrenalin effect). But once you stop playing or exercising, the blood glucose starts going back to the liver and muscle resulting in hypoglycaemia in the next 4-24 hours. This is called delayed hypoglycaemia. It should be kept in mind that the insulin dose has to be adjusted as per the sugar levels.

Sometimes hypos are seen in routine check-ups without any symptom. The first reason behind this is the slow drop of blood glucose (200-170-150-130, 100-70-50) and the second reason is the unawareness of hypoglycaemia.

In children with good sugar control, i.e. HbA1c levels around <6.5%, have less chances of hypo. But in our case, we give insulin without much thought which results in repetitive hypos thus adrenalin quantity reduces. Most of the parents have a misunderstanding that more insulin means normal HbA1c. But it is not true. More insulin means more hypos which is dangerous. Diabetes management is then like balancing yourself on a tight rope. If you learn to identify a hypo, prevent it and manage it then the rope balance becomes easy

sections.heading: Managing a hypo
sections.paragraph:
Mark Roofinact was detected with diabetes at the age of 28. As it was Type 1 diabetes, insulin was the only option. His paternal aunt lost her eye because of diabetes so Mark took care of his diabetes very strictly from the very beginning. Most of the time his blood glucose was normal so there were more hypo incidences. As he was aware of it and he had complete knowledge about diabetes he could prevent severe hypoglycaemia, but unknown stress was always there. Once Mark went to New York with his pet dog Armstrong. Mark was woken up by his dog Armstrong as he was all sweating, and his glucose level was <50. Armstrong helped Mark to identify his hypo and prevented a serious situation from occurring.

Mark researched his experience and started an organization named "dogs for diabetes" for the benefit of children with diabetes. In this organization, Labrador dogs were trained to understand hypo symptoms in children. This hypo companion will let his owner (T1D) know about their hypos in different ways and relax only when the owner eats glucose or sweet. After this, in research, it has been seen that your untrained but smart pet dog can also help in preventing hypos. Maybe your behavioural changes or change in body odour due to hypo is identified by your pet dog. One can keep dogs in their house as their hypo companion.

To monitor glucose levels in blood especially to identify a hypo, a new technology is developed called CGMS (continuous glucose monitoring system). A tiny sensor is inserted under your skin and every 5 minutes glucose level is shown to the insulin pump screen (real-time). It can also be sent wirelessly to your parent's monitor. CGMS continuously records your glucose level, if your glucose level goes down <70, it gives you a danger alarm. The hypo in the night can be recognised by the use of CGMS and can be immediately managed. Night-time hypos can cause irregular heartbeat resulting in serious problems. In developed countries, children use CGMS to manage their glucose level and prevent hypos.

Although this technical CGMS may not be affordable for everyone but one can still have a fair idea of their levels by monitoring BG levels with a glucometer and by keeping an accurate record of it. Keeping a record of how your blood glucose changes because of diet, insulin or exercise is important. This helps in having a 'Think Ahead' policy with your Diabetes team. The best understanding of your diabetes is the answer to prevent hypos.

What to do post hypo?

On your first visit, the diabetes team gives you complete information about what to do post hypo. An unwritten rule to this is to give sugar in any form as soon as possible. If the symptoms of a hypo are mild check your blood glucose, if it is not possible to give sugar or fruit juice. Temporarily high blood glucose will not make you sick so do not worry about that. Excessive glucose in the blood will be released out of the body through urine. Hypo can be severe if not controlled in time, so immediate action is compulsory. All children with Type 1 diabetes should keep some form of sweets with them like sugar, glucose, hypo tabs or glucovita. Chocolate can also be kept but young children might eat it without a hypo. When in hypo eat sugar, which is absorbed faster and raises the sugar levels in the blood. Normally within 15 to 20 minutes glucose level in blood increases, in that time period children need to be calm and composed.

After that initial time frame children can eat something heavy.

Some people follow the rule of 15 grams, which is to eat 15-gram carbs and check the blood sugar level in 15 minutes. If the glucose level is <70 then again take 15-gram carbs. Normally 4-5 mg glucose in the blood increases with one gram of carbs.

Question - if after hypo blood glucose level is 40 mg, how much sugar is required to make it 100 mg?

Answer - 1-gram sugar increases blood sugar level by 5 mg then (100-40)/5 = 60/5 = 12 gm sugar required.

If you have a spoon of 3 grams in your home, then 3-4 spoon sugar is required.

If you know, how and in what quantity your blood glucose increases then extreme ups and downs of blood glucose level can be prevented.

  1. Sugar - 2 or 3 spoons or make a syrup of it

  2. Glucose powder - blood glucose will increase immediately 2-3 spoons

  3. Honey one big spoon (15 ml)

  4. Fruit juice half Cup

  5. Hypo tabs - tablet of 4-gram easy to give to school going kids

  6. Cold drink - if the child is not ready to eat anything then only give half Cup

  7. Dates/Pomegranate - for mild hypo, one full fist.

Milk/Ice cream/Cadbury - with these blood glucose does not increase immediately but to avoid night-time hypo (2-3 am) it can be given before sleep.

Severe hypoglycaemia can cause unconsciousness in children. In this condition most of the people make a paste of glucose and apply it in the mouth which can work sometimes. But if this paste goes into the windpipe of an unconscious child it may give more trouble to the child. In this condition Glucagon injection is compulsory. But due to short expiry most of the time Glucagon is not available easily. You need to learn from your diabetes team about how to prepare Glucagon injection. As you know insulin syringes so you can easily inject through it.

1 gm glucagon injection

100-unit insulin syringe (orange cap)

1mg = 100 ml

Severe hypo

<6 yr child = 30 unit

6-15 yr child = 50 unit

>15 yr child=100 unit

Mini glucagon injection

Mild hypo

<2 yr child = 2 unit

3-15 yr child= 3-15 unit (year wise)

>15 yr child = 15 unit

If Glucagon is not available, then get hospitalised to the nearest hospital and intravenous glucose injection is compulsory. Sometimes if hypo is not severe but if you vomit or are not able to eat, in that case you can use a mini dose of Glucagon. A 100-unit insulin syringe gives 2-unit Glucagon to < 2-year children and in > 2-year children gives the same amount of Glucagon as their age. If blood glucose does not increase in 15 minutes you can repeat the dose. Mini Glucagon injection does not harm, and its effect is good.

sections.heading: How to prevent a hypo
sections.paragraph:
When on insulin, hypo fear is constant. Good control of diabetes means more chances of hypo. But that does not mean you keep eating or take insufficient insulin dose. How to fix insulin dose, complete diet information, the effect of exercise/game on your blood glucose- this all information is the answer to good control of diabetes.

Almost all children experience a mild hypo. If you inspect properly then you will find specific symptoms of your hypo. Do not neglect that. To prevent severe hypoglycaemia focus on your mild hypo. Some children do not understand mild hypo which is called 'hypoglycaemia unawareness'. In this situation, to know the symptoms of hypo it is necessary to prevent hypo for 2-3 weeks. Consult your diabetes team and increase your blood glucose target. If your blood glucose target is 100 make it 140-180 and most important take insulin dose very carefully.

You do not realise night-time hypos (2-3:00 AM) because of your deep sleep. If you are taking

NPH insulin (green label) in the night, then check your blood glucose in the night between 2-3:00 AM. Most of the time at this time glucose level can go down and then in the early morning due to counter-regulatory hormones blood glucose starts rising. That is why your blood glucose levels are high in the morning and you may not feel fresh. Depending upon early morning blood glucose if you increase NPH insulin dose then the intensity of hypo will also increase more. So, to answer this- 1. Decrease NPH insulin dose. 2. Start new basal insulin (Lantus/Levemir) 3. Before you sleep eat cheese bread or ice cream or 2 spoons raw custard with milk/curd. Sometimes medications with terbutaline increase blood glucose so to prevent night-time hypo this medicine (some cough syrup contains terbutaline) is used. Those children who play a lot in the evening may experience delayed hypoglycaemia. So, before dinner bolus dose or correction bolus dose needs to be decreased as per your glucose record (SMBG).

When the child experiences repetitive hypo but his glucose record does not show any problem then some tests have to be done. If possible, use CGMS to record hypo events. If some hormones are deficient or autoimmunity of gluten happens then the child can experience unexpected severe hypoglycaemia.

It has been proved that repetitive hypos can affect young children (6 years) in their emotional and mental growth. Therefore, hypo needs to be prevented.

There is a lot of research going on how to control blood glucose without hypo. Among them, some of the technology is being used in the clinical field.

  1. CGMS-there are so many CGMS available in the market by different pharmaceutical companies like Medtronic. With a sensor under the skin, every 5-minute glucose level can be seen. There is new research in this as per Raman spectroscopy a new band has been developed by which without pricking every 5-minute blood glucose is seen on the machine.

  2. Artificial pancreas- a program has been developed in the insulin pump to make it fully automatic. In this, there is an arrangement of giving Glucagon too. On an experimental basis at a few places, this is being used.

  3. Insulin analogues - effect of these insulins is like healthy body insulin. Some companies are manufacturing this kind of insulin and are available in the market. Research is going on smart insulin, in which depending on glucose level, insulin gets secreted from a chemical bond.

  4. Rational way - There is a lot of research going on like the islet cell transplant, Beta-cell production from stem cell or insulin gene to be placed in the pancreas for producing insulin within the body only. But not a single research is proved till date.

Dr Elliot Joslin has explained diabetes with a picture in which 3 horses are pulling a cart. These 3 horses are diet, exercise and insulin carrying the diabetes cart. Keeping a check on these 3 horses is not possible only with smartness or intelligence but it needs a team approach.

In OPD we understand that the main problem in diabetes control is fear of hypo which is very true but if you share your hypo incidence openly with your Diabetes team and make them a partner in your problem, you will find an answer to a lot of your problems and achieve good control. Your diabetes cart will not go haywire and you can win over it for lifetime.

Source: Dr. Kalpana Jog (MD-Pediatrics), T1D Consultant, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. Originally published in ‘Madhumitra’, a magazine of the Diabetic Association of India.
